subject: Request: downtime chronology, traces, and SLA remedy plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@cartwheelpay.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Checkout failures: increased 503 rate (02:12–02:18 UTC)

Hi Alex,

We saw a spike of 503s on our checkout endpoint during a five-minute window this morning (02:12–02:18 UTC). Our monitoring shows ~12% failed checkouts in that interval; overall throughput was normal but error rate spiked. Attached are a small sample of request IDs and raw traces we pulled from our edge.

Business impact: ~1.8k impacted transactions in the window, several merchants reported payment failures which we had to retry. This is the first time we've seen this pattern in production.

Can you confirm whether this maps to an incident on Redwood's side, and whether this window qualifies for SLA remediation? We need a short chronology and whether you can provide traces/RCAs for our auditors.

Attachments: cartwheel-sample-requests-20281116.jsonl (sample requests), billing-snapshot-20281116.csv (impact snapshot)

Thanks,
Samir
Ops Lead, Cartwheel Payments

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cartwheelpay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures: increased 503 rate (02:12–02:18 UTC)

Samir — thanks for the heads up and for attaching samples. I’ve looped in Laura (SRE) and Rishi (Customer Success / Billing) so we can triage quickly.

Initial asks from our side:
- Can you paste 2–3 concrete request IDs from the sample file that you want prioritized?
- Do you have full request/response headers for any of those IDs (we’ll need them to match traces)?
- Is there a preferred SLA remedy cadence you expect (summary + credit calculation, or full RCAs)?

Short plan: Laura will search our trace/dispatcher logs for the matching request IDs and confirm whether the errors were returned by our service or upstream (load balancer / preflight). If it’s within an availability window that meets the SLA failure definition, we’ll surface an eligibility assessment and a proposed credit calculation.

We’ll also upload any kernel-level traces we find to a shared Drive folder and include a short chronology. I’ll follow up within 90 minutes with an initial status.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cartwheelpay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 14:42:00 -08:00
Subject: SLA adjudication: chronology, evidence uploaded, and proposed next steps

Samir / Cartwheel team —

Quick update and formalization of next steps. Laura completed an initial trace correlation and we have evidence uploaded to the Drive folder below. Summary:

1) Chronology (UTC):
- 02:11:43 — small ramp of traffic, normal routing
- 02:12:04–02:18:11 — elevated 503s observed at the application dispatcher for a subset of shards; failure rate peaked at 14.8% around 02:15:30
- 02:18:12 — dispatcher recovered to baseline; no config deploys during window

2) Root cause (initial):
- Preliminary SRE analysis indicates a transient thread-pool starvation on the inference dispatcher while one shard experienced a delayed KV-cache lookup; this caused a cascade of short-lived 503 responses for inbound HTTP requests. We have kernel-level traces that show extended syscall wait on that shard during the window.

3) Evidence bundle uploaded:
- https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBexampleSLAevidence (kernel traces, dispatcher logs, sample request mappings)
- Attachments: kernel-traces-20281116.tar.gz (uploaded), cartwheel-sample-requests-20281116.jsonl (from you)

4) SLA eligibility assessment (preliminary):
- The window appears to meet our definition of an availability incident for the affected shard(s). We will run a formal eligibility calculation (pro-rata credit) per Section 4.2 of your contract and Redwood’s SLA policy. Rishi will draft the proposed credit amount and the accounting entry for your billing team.

5) Proposed next steps and timeline:
- 14:45 PST — Laura to deliver final trace mapping and confirm whether any requests were retried client-side (affects net impact).
- 16:00 PST — Rishi to provide the proposed credit calculation and a short summary of how the figure was derived.
- Within 72 hours — joint technical postmortem with Cartwheel (Redwood will prepare the draft RCA and invite your engineering leads).

If you prefer to escalate this to a formal claim ticket that triggers the SLA review playbook, tell us and we’ll convert this thread into a claim and fast-track the finance signoffs.

We apologize for the disruption and will include a concise RCA and the remediation steps we’ve already applied (thread-pool guardrails and additional KV-cache timeouts) in the postmortem.

Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199
